title: Ram Gopal Varma Reunites Satya Cast for Police Company, a Daya Nayak Biopic
excerpt: The T-Series-backed crime thriller stars Harshvardhan Rane as Mumbai's legendary encounter specialist, with Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, and Fardeen Khan rounding out the ensemble. Shooting begins today in Mumbai.
body:
• Ram Gopal Varma's Police Company, produced by T-Series, stars Harshvardhan Rane as Mumbai encounter specialist Daya Nayak and begins shooting on August 17 in Mumbai.
  • The ensemble includes Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, and Makarand Deshpande — reuniting three key actors from RGV's 1998 classic Satya — alongside Fardeen Khan and Soundarya Sharma.
  • Set between 1997 and 2004, the film chronicles a police squad believed to have eliminated nearly 300 gangsters during Mumbai's peak underworld era.
  • Production aims to wrap by December 2026, with a theatrical release planned for 2027.

Ram Gopal Varma is returning to the genre that defined his career. The filmmaker has officially begun production on Police Company, a period crime thriller based on the life of former Mumbai encounter specialist Daya Nayak, with Harshvardhan Rane in the lead role. Shooting commenced on August 17 in Mumbai, backed by Bhushan Kumar's T-Series and RGV's own production banner.

From Mangalore to Mumbai's Frontlines

Police Company traces Daya Nayak's trajectory from a small village in Mangalore to the upper ranks of the Mumbai Police, where he became one of India's most recognised encounter specialists. Between 1997 and 2004, a special squad within the Mumbai Police was formed to counter the rapidly expanding underworld — a unit that RGV has described as "more dangerous than D Company." The squad is believed to have eliminated nearly 300 gangsters during that period.

"My next film's name being produced by T-Series is Police Company. With the tag line 'It Is More Dangerous Than D Company.'"

— Ram Gopal Varma, via social media

Varma has long been fascinated by Nayak's career. He previously produced Ab Tak Chhappan (2004), in which Nana Patekar played a character inspired by the encounter specialist. Police Company, however, is positioned as a deeper exploration — a full biopic rather than a loosely inspired narrative.

A Satya Reunion and Fresh Faces

The casting is a deliberate callback to RGV's golden era. Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, and Makarand Deshpande — three actors who delivered career-defining performances in Satya (1998) — have been enlisted for pivotal supporting roles. Fardeen Khan joins as a key member of the police squad, while Soundarya Sharma plays the female lead opposite Rane.

For Harshvardhan Rane, whose last major appearance was in Ek Deewane Ki Deewaniyat (2025), the role represents a significant career pivot. His first-look stills, shared by RGV on social media, show a striking physical transformation modelled closely on Daya Nayak's real appearance.

RGV's Crime Legacy

Police Company extends Varma's long-standing engagement with Mumbai's criminal underworld, following Satya (1998), Company (2002), and D Company (2021). While the title evokes the franchise, the new film is entirely standalone — this time the camera shifts from the gangsters to the police officers who hunted them.

The project gained momentum after RGV's other crime thriller, Syndicate, failed to materialise due to budgetary constraints. With T-Series providing large-scale backing — marking the first collaboration between Bhushan Kumar and Varma — Police Company is being mounted as a mainstream theatrical release.

What's Next

Production is scheduled to wrap by December 2026, with a theatrical release targeted for 2027. For Indian cinema audiences and diaspora viewers who grew up on RGV's gritty Mumbai crime dramas, Police Company promises a return to the filmmaker's most potent territory — this time grounded in documented police history rather than fictional underworld mythology.
